name: AI back office · Invoices, bank lines and questions

parameters.content:
## AI back office · Invoices, bank lines and questions
Agents read supplier invoices from Gmail, code them against the chart of accounts and file them in QuickBooks. Bank lines are matched every morning, the ledger is scanned for anomalies, finance can ask questions in Slack, and the month closes into a Google Sheets pack. Every figure is checked or computed in code.

**Platforms:** Gmail, OpenAI, Supabase, Claude, Pinecone, QuickBooks, Slack, Google Sheets
**Source and tests:** github.com/kimjoshuadr/n8n-workflows · `systems/ai-back-office`

nodes.name: Section: Invoice intake: read, check, code, file

parameters.content:
## 1. Invoice intake: read, check, code, file
A model copies the fields. Code checks the document's own arithmetic and the vendor's history before anything reaches QuickBooks.

## 2. Bank matching
Exact matches in code first. An agent proposes the rest; equal amounts and confidence decide.

## 3. Anomaly watch
Fixed rules raise the flags. The agent only orders and explains them.

## 4. Questions in Slack
Read-only tools, a calculator, and no answer without the rows behind it.

options.systemMessage: You are the Extraction agent. Copy the fields of this supplier invoice exactly as written: vendor name, invoice number, invoice date and due date as YYYY-MM-DD, currency, each line with its amount, subtotal, tax, total, and the bank account or IBAN to pay if one is printed. Use null for anything not on the document. Never work a number out: copy it.

nodes.name: What we know of the vendor

options.systemMessage: You are the Coding agent. Choose the expense account for this invoice from the chart of accounts. Search the chart first and answer with an account name exactly as it appears there. If the vendor has a default account and the lines fit it, use it. Give your confidence.

parameters.toolDescription: Search the chart of accounts and the notes on what belongs in each account.

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ VendorRef: { name: $json.vendor }, DocNumber: $json.invoice_number, TxnDate: $json.invoice_date, DueDate: $json.due_date, CurrencyRef: { value: $json.currency }, Line: [{ Amount: $json.total, DetailType: 'AccountBasedExpenseLineDetail', AccountBasedExpenseLineDetail: { AccountRef: { name: $json.account } } }] }) }}

options.systemMessage: You are the Matching agent. Some bank lines did not match a bill exactly. For each bank line, say which open bill it most likely pays, if any, and why: a vendor name in the memo, a reference that is nearly the invoice number. Propose a match only when the amounts are equal. Give a confidence for each.

parameters.text: ={{ ':bank: Matched ' + $('Accept only what holds up').first().json.matched.length + ' bank lines to bills. ' + ($('Accept only what holds up').first().json.exceptions.length ? $('Accept only what holds up').first().json.exceptions.length + ' could not be matched: ' + $('Accept only what holds up').first().json.exceptions.map(e => e.amount + ' "' + e.memo + '"').join('; ') : 'Nothing left unmatched.') }}

options.systemMessage: You are the Anomaly agent. These invoices were flagged by fixed rules. For a finance manager, put them in order of how much they deserve a look and say in one line each what to check. Do not add flags of your own and do not say anything is fraud.

parameters.text: ={{ ':warning: ' + $('Look for the unusual').first().json.flags.length + ' invoice(s) look unusual.\n' + ($('Anomaly agent').first().json.output ?? $('Look for the unusual').first().json.flags.map(f => f.vendor + ' ' + f.invoice_number + ': ' + f.kind).join('\n')) }}

parameters.responseBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ response_type: 'ephemeral', text: 'Sorry, only the finance team can ask about the books.' }) }}

options.systemMessage: You are the Analyst agent for a finance team. Answer questions about supplier invoices from the ledger. Always query the ledger before answering, and add numbers up with the calculator, never in your head. Reply with the answer in one or two sentences, the figures you used, and which rows they came from. If the ledger cannot answer the question, say so. You can read; you cannot pay, change or delete anything.

parameters.toolDescription: Reads supplier invoices from the ledger. Columns: vendor, invoice_number, total, currency, due_date, account, status (awaiting_payment or paid), at.
parameters.filterString: ={{ $fromAI('filter', `A PostgREST filter, for example status=eq.awaiting_payment or vendor=eq.Acme Supplies. Leave empty for all rows.`, 'string') }}

parameters.description: Adds a list of numbers. Pass them separated by commas.
parameters.jsCode: const n = String(query).split(',').map((x) => Number(x.trim())).filter(Number.isFinite); return String(Math.round(n.reduce((a, b) => a + b, 0) * 100) / 100);

parameters.responseBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ response_type: 'in_channel', text: $('Only answer with working').first().json.text }) }}

options.systemMessage: You are the Close agent. Write the month-end note for the owner: three sentences on what was spent and what changed against the month before, then up to three things worth a question. Use only the figures given, and quote them exactly.

parameters.text: ={{ ':ledger: *' + $('Total by account').first().json.month + ' closed.* Spend ' + $('Total by account').first().json.total + ' (prior month ' + $('Total by account').first().json.prior_total + '). ' + $('Total by account').first().json.unpaid_count + ' bills unpaid, ' + $('Total by account').first().json.unpaid_total + '.\n' + ($('Close agent').first().json.output?.summary ?? 'The written note is unavailable; the figures are in the pack.') }}
